title: LLM throughput smoke harness + regression watch for core models
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build and maintain a compact, CI-friendly tokens-per-second (TPS) smoke harness that exercises our core model serving stack and feeds a lightweight regression detector. The goal is to catch regressions in sustained throughput and p95 token latency early (nightly/nightly-canary) while remaining cheap and stable enough to run on PRs for infra changes. This complements existing heavy-load suites by providing fast feedback on: model kernel regressions, kv-cache behavior, batching changes, and routing/serve config impacts.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke harness runs in < 20 minutes for full model matrix on our CI GPU pool
Produces stable per-model TPS and p95 baseline artifacts stored in S3 and indexed by commit
Automatic regression detector triggers an alert if TPS drops >5% or p95 increases >10% vs baseline for any model/seq-length profile
Results are visible in the runtime-performance dashboard and a compact PR comment summarizing pass/fail
Harness includes at least 3 sequence-length profiles (short:64, medium:512, long:1536) and kv-cache warmup flow
tasks: Design harness test runner and minimal model matrix (list of core models and quant/float variants)
Instrument p95 token-latency and sustained-tps measurement with token-aligned timing
Add kv-cache warmup routine and prefix-caching toggle to simulate real traffic patterns
Implement regression detector service that compares latest runs to stored baselines and emits Slack/Grafana alerts
Integrate harness into CI: PR-smoke (fast, subset), nightly-full (complete matrix)
Create dashboard panels for tps/p95 trends and per-run diffs, link from PRs
notes: We intentionally keep harness lightweight: target ~3-5 model variants per run so PRs can run in ~10 minutes using smaller batch sizes and sample inputs.
Sequence-length choices reflect typical production mix: 64 for chat turns, 512 for summaries, 1536 to stress KV/cache and attention kernels.
Regression thresholds tuned conservatively to reduce noise: initial TPS threshold = 5% drop, p95 threshold = 10% increase. We will iterate after 2 weeks of telemetry.
Avoids synthetic max-fill loads used by stress benches; instead uses steady-stream generation to measure sustained tokens/sec under normal batching behaviors.
Potential false positives when infra upgrades change kernel selection - include commit metadata and node-flavor tags in baselines to narrow scope.
